problem: VLMs produce unstable trajectories when predicting navigation paths directly from a single egocentric observation. World-model-generated futures are visually plausible but give no grounded signal for trajectory learning, and using them as test-time evidence can hurt.
motivation: Reliable mapless trajectory prediction toward semantic targets matters for embodied navigation, but classical mapping pipelines need persistent maps and exploration. Generated views are often cross-view inconsistent, so consuming them directly can mislead (MindJourney underperforms direct o3). The paper instead uses generated futures to build structured supervision.
key_idea: Use a world-model-driven teacher that turns generated future videos into semantic-spatial memory, target and obstacle grounding, and a cost-BEV FMM plan, then distill these planning-derived trajectory pseudo-labels into a lightweight VLM student with a multi-hypothesis head.
insight: World models are more useful as supervision engines than as test-time evidence. Direct VLM prediction and MindJourney (o3, ADE 152.41) are far worse than the distilled student (ADE 42.06). The supervision ablation shows GT only (ADE 78.34) and WM pseudo-labels only (ADE 95.98) are both poor, while combining GT with filtered pseudo-labels gives 42.06. Backbone scale matters little (4B 45.07 vs 8B 42.06), so the supervision recipe dominates.
method: Future video generation: multiple streams of world-model-generated future videos from a single first-person RGB image provide complementary nearby viewpoints.

3D reconstruction and semantic-spatial memory: Depth Anything 3 gives per-frame depth and camera pose. Each frame is stored with a visual embedding, caption and pose, and a RANSAC ground plane defines the shared navigation plane.

Task-aware grounding: CLIP retrieves relevant memory frames. A VLM writes a target phrase and proposes obstacle categories, and UniPixel-7B segments them. Masks are filtered with a VLM mask judge, fused in 3D and projected to BEV.

Cost-BEV and FMM planning: An RGB BEV (5 mm per cell, height band -0.5 to +1.5 m) is overlaid with target and obstacle regions. Obstacles and unobserved background are blocked, safety margins carry higher costs, and Fast Marching finds a path that is smoothed and resampled into waypoints.
Pseudo-label quality filtering: A VLM judge rates trajectories on task success, stop accuracy, collision safety, naturalness and cross-view consistency, and labels them usable, borderline or reject.
Student: Qwen3-VL-8B with a LoRA adapter (stage A) plus a lightweight decoder (stage B; hidden dim 256, 3 MLP layers, 8 cross-attention heads) that predicts K trajectory hypotheses with confidences.
Student loss: L2 waypoint error plus a direction cosine consistency term (lambda_d=0.5) with best-of-K min over hypotheses; AdamW, lr 5e-4, 100 epochs.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B student (LoRA plus trajectory decoder, trained); teacher uses frozen world models, Depth Anything 3, CLIP, UniPixel-7B and a VLM
setting.training_data: Teacher-generated FMM trajectory pseudo-labels from world-model futures on Target-Bench train scenes, combined with Target-Bench train GT trajectories (usable pseudo-labels only in the main model)
setting.observation: single first-person monocular RGB image plus language instruction
setting.action_space: multi-hypothesis future waypoint trajectory in 2D image space (best-of-K, one selected at inference)
setting.privileged: none at test time (teacher is used only in training; training additionally uses benchmark GT)

numbers_note: The paper does not name the Target-Bench split explicitly. The supplementary mentions a 'processed validation split', so 'val' is used. Metrics are pixel-space ADE/FDE/DTW, not SR/SPL.
results: On Target-Bench, WorldMAP reaches ADE 42.06 and FDE 38.87, versus the best baseline Gemini-3-Pro at 51.27 and 67.19 (an 18.0% ADE and 42.1% FDE reduction), with DTW near-equal (31.95 vs 31.63). It far outperforms open-source VLMs used directly (Qwen3-VL-8B ADE 183.93) and MindJourney (152.41).
limitations: Evaluated only on Target-Bench; transfer to dynamic scenes, multi-level environments and long-horizon exploration is untested.
The teacher depends on the quality of world-model generation and geometric reconstruction; generations can be inconsistent or hallucinated.
The gain cannot be attributed to supervision alone, since the teacher also contributes retrieval, grounding and planning.
